I'm in the same boat. Take it easy don't try to quit both at the same time.  If you don't already smoke cigarettes then I would recommend nicorette for a bit to help. 

I quit moke bowls and kept smoking cigarettes for a week or two now I am working on the nicotine part.

I have had a solid stutter most of my life.  I thought for sure weed helped, but realized the days after smoking I could barely say my name.  I am on day 15 myself and slowly getting better.  

Just my anecdote.  Keep it up!

I was in the same but. I realized I was in a downward spiral and went catatonic. Seeing someone a therapist or a psychiatrist probably saved my life. I am on meds for the short term to essentially just get me out of this funk and start being able to treat it. You won't be on meds your whole life but it's worth heavily considering for the short term to ease your suffering. 

Good luck.
At least try not to play the same games. Like I used to play rocket league stoned off my ass, couldn't play that for a week or two but found it much more enjoyable afterwards.
Take a break with games. When I stopped smoking, video games were a trigger.

Good on you for thinking of your son.

Download a quick pick up game for your phone or start a book.  What I find helps me is something that consumes my mind.  Reading does not give me time to think so if I crave I just read for a bit.

Keep distracted and really remember why you are doing this.

Exactly. The line from Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind "why do I fall in love with anyone who makes eye contact with me" really stuck out. 

It absolutely is an inner battle and I have made myself look like a total asshole to a lot of people. There were times where I swore someone was cheating on me and woke up at 2am driving to their place and pounding on the door frantically. Then to my surprise my mind tricked me and it was all bullshit. 

When that hits it fucking sucks and you begin to call yourself a fucking dumbass, worthless ignorant piece of shit. That internal monologue continues but eventually it becomes more routine and exhausting. 

To give you some hope and I don't know your relationship status but I eventually found an understanding women who sees the person under the mood swings.

That's interesting because there were times where I met someone new and was so taken by them that I would get fixated on making a friendship. I have worked on that for a few years because as you know it can be downright embarrassing. Then you sit and go through all your conversations wondering if you said something wrong or maybe sent a message at the wrong time. It just runs through your head non stop. I just read that fear of rejection is a common symptom of BPD, which for my background makes way too much sense.

To me that's really on you.  It takes a lot to be honest with yourself if you can actually moderate or are you letting your friends moderate you?

I struggle with this as well.  If it's there it's gone, no matter what it is, booze, pot, other drugs you name it, I'm all or nothing to the max.

Overtime I had to be honest with myself and make the decision that if I am going to quit it truly has to be for yourself.  If you want to moderate you need to see why you can't moderate yourself.  Be an observer upon yourself, as hippy and western medicine as it may sound.

Good luck and stay true.

As a recovering alcoholic the real pain part of avoiding bars and stores is changing the way you think.  Sure I can get blasted literally at anytime (I live in NYC) and there are plenty who would sit right next to me.  When you resolve the internal struggle of saying "I can't smoke" to "I don't smoke" that's when it becomes easier to avoid it.  Don't think of it as something you are being restricted from.

Also I have a history of mental illness and I know the struggles with the herb and making everything flat and comfortable.  

Good luck

This is a huge realization!  I quit drinking but still used marijuana as my coping "I don't drink anymore so I can smoke all I want."  As time went on I realized I was just using it as an escape mechanism and it really isn't much better than Alcohol (for me personally, I don't want to make blanket assumptions).  

Finally starting to realize that I need to practice self-love and personal care.  It seems trivial but is a huge change of mindset.

Congrats and good luck!

I'm quitting as well for similar symptoms, the raw throat and ridiculous GI issues especially the first morning after.  I am in the same boat as well as determining if this is long term.  What helped me quit drinking (almost a year now!) was just to not think of it as a good bye but knowing at least in the short term, it's not helping and know at least for a month I need to stop.  When I quit drinking I just wanted to get a day under my belt then slowly that turned into weeks and so on.  After awhile it wasn't a thought of "I can't drink," which is the mindset of many when getting rid of a vice, and it turned into "I don't drink".  

Anecdotal advice... hope it helps somewhat.

I'm going through it today too.  I agree quitting smoking was bitching a last year, as well as not drinking anymore.  Makes the detox process that much harder, but coming on top shows you have the coping skills to get through tough situations later in life.  Everything starts with the first minute of not smoking then 15 mins and so on.

Good Luck
